text.p: German armaments maker Rheinmetall AG, which on Thursday led a consortium taking over defence electronics company STN Atlas Elektronik, said sales would grow this year and it would post a healthy profits increase.
In a regulatory news release, the company said it expected group sales to rise by 4.8 percent to 3.6 billion marks, while order intake would jump 16.9 percent to 4.2 billion marks.
The company also said it expected to post a net profit running into double-digit millions of marks, up from six million marks last year.
Rheinmetall headed a group with Badenwerk AG and British Aerospace which on Thursday signed a contract with the official receiver to buy STN Atlas, a unit of the defunct Bremer Vulkan shipyard group.

Rheinmetall will with Badenwerk own 51 percent of STN Atlas, while BAe takes 49 percent. It will have executive control over STN Atlas, bought for 550 million marks, and said the acquisition would have a positive impact on 1997 earnings.
